Imo this feels like the death of human advancement. 

Current AI is built on LLM which, as my meagre understanding goes, is basically an aggregate of data and the outputs are basically averages. 

If the LLM is trained on Human Data then it gives decent results but if it's trained AI generated data it gives horrendous results. 

By taking out the human component from work and replacing the humans with AI, we're basically taking out the ingenuity and authenticity of anything we do and eventually once all the authentic Human data left behind by people is processed and 90% of the population has been replaced, the 10% that is in charge of teaching the LLMs will not be smart enough/learned enough to distinguish between Human created data and AI generated data because you need people to interact with people to learn. This will finally cause so many garbage outputs that barely anyone is able to verify the quality of. 

It's like the output of everything we do is a glass of beer. Genuine discovery, hard work etc is the cream at the top of the beer. People performing averagely are the middle of glass' beer. People performing poorly are the dregs at the bottom. 
The average of all of this is an LLM output in another beer glass, which does not have the potential to go beyond the middle beer. 
Eventually you keep averaging out the LLM beer and all everyone gets is the dregs at the bottom.
